topics.question: Why does scanning a document not complete digital preservation?

topics.question: How can libraries serve users whose access needs differ from standard print?

topics.question: What makes a born-digital collection difficult to preserve authentically?
topics.coverage: Trace software dependencies and changing file environments.

topics.question: How can archives document a gap without inventing the missing history?
topics.coverage: Separate known absence, destruction and unprocessed materials.

topics.question: How do metadata and preservation formats serve different archival functions?
topics.coverage: Separate discovery, representation and long-term access.

topics.question: Why do reading-room rules and digitization copyright determine different kinds of access?
topics.coverage: Map institutional policy and legal questions.

topics.question: How can catalog bias and donation provenance shape whose records survive?
topics.coverage: Trace collection decisions and missing archives.

topics.question: How can a community library define success beyond circulation totals?
topics.coverage: Compare community priorities, access, languages and sustained participation in one setting.

topics.question: How should an archive prioritize continuity when a disaster damages both collections and its catalog?
topics.coverage: Map dependency records, qualified conservation decisions and staged access without salvage procedures.

topics.question: How did the British Library restore collection discovery and access after its October 2023 cyber incident?
topics.coverage: Read the British Library?s March 2024 incident review and dated interim-catalog/access notices as an institutional continuity case. Separate survival of collection data from working catalog, request and reading-room services; distinguish 2024 recovery stages from later status. Focus on archive access decisions, not attack mechanics or security instructions.

topics.question: Why can an archived webpage preserve its appearance while losing important interactions?
topics.coverage: Trace linked resources, dynamic content, capture dates and documented gaps.

topics.question: What makes removing an item from a collection an accountability decision rather than routine housekeeping?
topics.coverage: Compare mission, provenance, restrictions, consultation and transparent disposition records.
